questions.problem:
Given that $A=QR$ is a QR factorization of a $4\times 3$ matrix $A$ with linearly independent columns, which of the following statements are true?

I. The columns of $Q$ are orthogonal

II. $Q$ is a $4\times 3$ matrix

III. $R$ is a $4\times 3$ matrix
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A=QR$ is a  QR factorization of an $m\times n$ matrix $A,$ then

$$
{A}_{m\times n}={Q}_{m\times n}\times {R}_{n\times n},
$$

where 

- $Q$ is an $m\times n$ matrix whose columns form an orthonormal basis of $\text{Col}(A)$

- $R$ is an $n\times n$ upper triangular matrix

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Since the columns of $Q$ form an orthonormal basis, they are orthogonal.

- Statement II is true. Indeed, $Q$ must be a $4\times 3$ matrix.

- Statement III is false. $R$ should be a $3\times 3$ upper triangular matrix.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

questions.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained from the columns of $A$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, find  the value of ${q}_{11}\cdot {r}_{12}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ be the columns of $A.$

First, we find an orthonormal basis of $\text{Col}(A)=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**. We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**. We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}\{{v}_{1}\}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 8\end{aligned}]-\frac{24}{12}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 8\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we normalize ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3} & 4\sqrt{3} \\ 0 & 4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3} & 4\sqrt{3} \\ 0 & 4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Finally, ${q}_{12}\cdot {r}_{22}=(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})\cdot (4\sqrt{3})=-4.$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained from the columns of $A$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, find  the value of ${q}_{22}\cdot {r}_{22}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ be the columns of $A.$

First, we find an orthonormal basis of $\text{Col}(A)=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**. We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**. We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}\{{v}_{1}\}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{6}{12}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we normalize ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3} & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & 0\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3} & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Finally, ${q}_{22}\cdot {r}_{22}=(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})\cdot (2\sqrt{2})=2.$

questions.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of ${q}_{32}\cdot {r}_{22}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the columns of $A$ are already orthogonal, to construct an orthogonal matrix $Q,$ we simply normalize ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ 0 & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Finally, ${q}_{32}\cdot {r}_{22}=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\cdot \sqrt{6}=-2.$
